followup: Re-measure after any workload change (e.g. larger DB, more traffic); limits are generous ceilings, not tuned reservations.

limits.method: docker update --memory 1g --memory-swap 1g for postgres/qdrant (no restart); docker run --memory 1g --memory-swap 1g for gateway (recreated)

rationale: Limits are 7-28x measured peak working sets: conservative containment against runaway growth, never close to normal operation. Total capped 3g of 5.765g leaves ample host headroom. Memswap equals memory (no swap on host anyway).
summary: Measured 10-minute steady-state working sets (10 samples per container, very flat: gateway 117.7-118.2 MiB, postgres 32.1-35.8 MiB, qdrant 48.6-52.9 MiB). Set 1g memory ceilings on all three containers. Postgres and qdrant updated live with no restart; gateway picked up the limit at recreation. Verified in docker stats and via docker inspect after a gateway restart: mem and memswap persist at 1073741824. Compose file annotated with the same limits (backup kept) for any future compose-based recreation.
